ru: v. to become less active, less intense, or less in amount
simple_examples: As I began my speech, my feelings of nervousness quickly abated.
The storm finally abated after several hours of heavy rain.
advanced_example: Once the initial excitement abated, the researchers were able to analyze the results more objectively.

ru: adj. Sudden and unexpected.
simple_examples: His abrupt departure surprised everyone.
The car came to an abrupt stop at the red light.
advanced_example: The experiment ended in an abrupt fashion when the machinery malfunctioned.

ru: adj. existing purely in the mind; not representing actual reality
simple_examples: Julie had trouble understanding the appeal of the abstract painting.
The teacher used a concrete example to explain the abstract idea.
advanced_example: The philosopher’s argument relies on abstract notions of justice rather than concrete legal codes.

ru: adj. extremely bad
simple_examples: I got an abysmal grade on my research paper!
The restaurant's service was absolutely abysmal.
advanced_example: Critics condemned the film for its abysmal writing and wooden acting.

ru: adj. Satisfactory or permissible.
simple_examples: The teacher deemed Sara's late assignment acceptable.
Your answer is acceptable, but it could be clearer.
advanced_example: Although not ideal, the compromise was acceptable to all parties involved.

ru: adj. Happening by chance.
simple_examples: The oil spill was purely accidental.
Their meeting at the café was completely accidental.
advanced_example: Investigators concluded that the damage was accidental rather than deliberate.

ru: v. To provide space or make adjustments.
simple_examples: The Grand Hotel can accommodate up to 500 guests.
We try to accommodate students with special needs.
advanced_example: The schedule was revised to accommodate the concerns raised by the faculty.

ru: n. The quality of being correct or precise.
simple_examples: The accuracy of the intern's report was impressive.
Good instruments improve the accuracy of measurements.
advanced_example: The accuracy of the historical records has been questioned by recent scholars.

ru: v. To recognize or admit the truth.
simple_examples: She refused to acknowledge her mistake.
The company finally acknowledged the problem with the product.
advanced_example: The author acknowledges the limitations of the study before presenting her conclusions.

ru: adj. Gained through effort or experience.
simple_examples: Edmund had acquired a taste for fine wine.
Language is partly innate and partly an acquired skill.
advanced_example: Her acquired expertise in data analysis made her an invaluable member of the research team.

ru: v. To adjust to new conditions.
simple_examples: Newly-released animals generally adapt to their environments over time.
It can be hard to adapt to a new school.
advanced_example: Societies must adapt their institutions to respond to rapid technological change.

ru: adj. having knowledge or skill (usu. in a particular area)
simple_examples: Beth loves playing the piano, but she’s especially adept at the violin.
He is adept at solving complex math problems.
advanced_example: An adept negotiator, she secured favorable terms without alienating the other side.

ru: adj. having sufficient qualifications to meet a specific task or purpose
simple_examples: Though his resume was adequate, the company doubted whether he’d be a good fit.
We have adequate food for the trip.
advanced_example: The report concludes that current funding is barely adequate to maintain existing services.

ru: v. To stick to or follow closely.
simple_examples: You must adhere to the rules if you don't want to get in trouble.
The labels did not adhere well to the boxes.
advanced_example: Despite criticism, the committee continued to adhere to its original guidelines.

ru: v. To modify or change slightly.
simple_examples: He had to adjust his seat for comfort.
You can adjust the volume with this knob.
advanced_example: The researchers adjusted their model to account for the new data.

ru: v. To respect or look up to.
simple_examples: I admire my mother's dedication to her work.
Many students admire that professor.
advanced_example: Historians continue to admire her courage in challenging the prevailing norms of her time.

ru: adj. Beneficial or useful.
simple_examples: Speaking multiple languages is advantageous.
Living near the school is advantageous for students.
advanced_example: The policy proved advantageous to small businesses, which gained access to new markets.

ru: n. the arrival or creation of something
simple_examples: The world has never been the same since the advent of the light bulb.
advanced_example: The advent of social media transformed how people consume news and interact with one another.

ru: v. To recommend or give guidance.
simple_examples: I advise you to study for the exam.
Doctors advise patients to get enough sleep.
advanced_example: The committee advised the council to postpone the vote until more data could be gathered.

ru: v. To worsen or intensify.
simple_examples: Scratching the rash will only aggravate it.
Loud noises can aggravate her headaches.

ru: adj. Forceful or overly assertive.
simple_examples: The man's aggressive tone made everyone uneasy.
Some salespeople can be very aggressive.
advanced_example: The company adopted an aggressive marketing strategy to gain market share quickly.

ru: v. to make a secretive mention of something
simple_examples: She alluded to the problem at hand but didn’t say anything more about it.
The author alludes to a famous myth in this chapter.
advanced_example: By alluding to earlier reforms, the speech situates the new law within a broader historical context.

ru: n. Uncertainty or multiple interpretations.
simple_examples: The ambiguity in his vague statement caused confusion.
Legal documents must avoid ambiguity.

ru: n. Mixed or conflicting feelings.
simple_examples: Jessie felt ambivalence about moving to a new city.
He spoke with ambivalence about his promotion.

ru: v. To improve or make better.
simple_examples: The new policy aims to ameliorate working conditions for all employees.
Proper ventilation can ameliorate the effects of pollution indoors.

ru: v. To increase in size or effect.
simple_examples: The microphone will amplify your voice.
Social media can amplify small disagreements into public conflicts.

ru: adj. Entertaining or humorous.
simple_examples: Jason's joke was quite amusing.
The movie was light and amusing.
advanced_example: Though seemingly amusing, the story contains a sharp critique of social norms.

ru: adj. similar but not identical
simple_examples: Green onions are considered analogous to spring onions.
The brain is sometimes described as analogous to a computer.

ru: v. To add notes or comments.
simple_examples: Please annotate the medical text with your observations.
Students were asked to annotate the poem as they read.
advanced_example: Scholars continue to annotate the manuscript, adding context for modern readers.

ru: v. To make a public statement.
simple_examples: The CEO will announce the new policy tomorrow.
They announced their engagement at dinner.

ru: n. something different from the norm
simple_examples: This result is an anomaly and very rarely happens.
advanced_example: The unusually high temperature reading was dismissed as an anomaly in the data.

ru: adj. Showing hostility or opposition.
simple_examples: His antagonistic behavior created tension at work.
The two politicians were openly antagonistic during the debate.
advanced_example: The novel portrays an antagonistic relationship between industrial progress and natural landscapes.

ru: n. A preceding event or condition.
simple_examples: The antecedent to the war was political unrest.
advanced_example: The author carefully traces the cultural antecedents of the modern movement.

ru: v. To expect or predict.
simple_examples: Does the weatherman anticipate a rise in temperatures next week?
We anticipate heavy traffic during the holiday weekend.
advanced_example: The policy was designed to anticipate demographic changes rather than merely react to them.

ru: n. a strong feeling of dislike
simple_examples: Her antipathy toward the professor was obvious: she rolled her eyes whenever he entered the classroom.
advanced_example: Public antipathy toward the proposal forced legislators to reconsider their plans.

ru: n. the highest point of something
simple_examples: The spring play was the apex of our school year.
advanced_example: The empire reached its apex under the reign of its most successful ruler.

ru: adj. Suitable for a specific situation.
simple_examples: Lily's velvet dress was appropriate for the formal occasion.

ru: adj. Nearly accurate or close to.
simple_examples: The approximate cost is $50.
We arrived at the approximate location on the map.

ru: adj. Mysterious or known by few.
simple_examples: The ancient book contained arcane knowledge.
Only a few experts understood the arcane rules of the game.

ru: adj. Difficult and requiring effort.
simple_examples: The steep hike up the mountain was arduous.
Studying for final exams can be an arduous task.
advanced_example: The project demanded an arduous combination of physical endurance and mental focus.

ru: v. To gather or put together.
simple_examples: We need to assemble the bed if we want a place to sleep tonight.
The students assembled in the auditorium.
advanced_example: The curator carefully assembled artifacts from around the world for the new exhibit.

ru: adj. extremely plain; adj. stern and forbidding; adj. relating to self-denial
simple_examples: He lived in a small, austere cabin in the middle of the woods.

An austere lifestyle, like that of monks, isn’t for everybody.
advanced_example: The government adopted an austere budget that cut nearly all nonessential programs.

ru: v. To stay away from or prevent.
simple_examples: Mara hates fighting, so she always tries to avoid conflict.
We left early to avoid traffic.

ru: adj. Producing good results.
simple_examples: A balanced diet is beneficial to your health.
Exercise is beneficial for mental well-being.
advanced_example: The study suggests that even small lifestyle changes can be highly beneficial over time.

ru: adj. kind, generous
simple_examples: Many cultures believe in benevolent spirits.
The benevolent donor paid for the new library.
advanced_example: The organization’s ostensibly benevolent mission masked its more self-serving goals.

ru: adj. Courageous or striking.
simple_examples: Elsie made a bold move by quitting her job.
The painting uses bold colors.
advanced_example: The scientist made a bold claim that challenged decades of accepted theory.

ru: v. To take temporarily.
simple_examples: Libraries will let you borrow books for several weeks.
Can I borrow your notes from class?

ru: v. To support or strengthen.
simple_examples: The evidence will buttress his argument.
New data buttressed the scientist's hypothesis.
advanced_example: The author marshals historical examples to buttress her central claim.

ru: v. To go around or avoid.
simple_examples: We took a shortcut to bypass traffic.
The engineers built a canal to bypass the dangerous rapids.

ru: v. To adjust for precision.
simple_examples: The scientist had to calibrate the instrument to ensure his measurements were accurate.
advanced_example: Before conducting the experiment, the team carefully calibrated each sensor.

ru: adj. direct, blunt
simple_examples: Josh is candid about his desire to become an actor.
Her candid response surprised the interviewer.
advanced_example: The memoir offers a candid account of the author’s struggles with failure.

ru: adv. Without caution.
simple_examples: He carelessly left his keys on the bus.
She carelessly spilled coffee on the report.
advanced_example: The chemicals were carelessly stored, creating a serious safety hazard.

ru: adj. Disastrous or causing great damage.
simple_examples: The catastrophic hurricane destroyed dozens of homes.
A catastrophic failure of the engine forced the plane to land.

ru: n. A reason for an action or event.
simple_examples: The fire's cause is still unknown.
Researchers are studying the cause of the disease.

ru: n. The way a character is described.
simple_examples: The novel's characterization was deep and complex.

ru: v. To find a way around.
simple_examples: They found a loophole to circumvent the rule.

ru: n. A surprising and unexpected event.
simple_examples: Meeting my neighbor at the airport was a coincidence.
It was no coincidence that sales rose after the ad campaign.

ru: n. Working together on a task.
simple_examples: The scientists' collaboration led to a breakthrough.
Group projects require good collaboration.
advanced_example: The success of the initiative depended on close collaboration between public and private institutions.

ru: n. The process of making something a business.
simple_examples: The commercialization of the product increased sales.
advanced_example: Critics argue that the commercialization of the holiday has overshadowed its original meaning.

ru: adj. Dedicated to a cause or task.
simple_examples: Ava is committed to her studies and always wants top grades.
The volunteers are committed to helping the community.
advanced_example: The organization relies on a small but highly committed group of activists.

ru: adj. Occurring frequently or shared.
simple_examples: It's very common for students to feel stressed before exams.
Sneezing is a common symptom of allergies.

ru: adj. Captivating or persuasive.
simple_examples: The debater gave a compelling argument.
The documentary was compelling from start to finish.
advanced_example: The data present a compelling case for reevaluating current policies.

ru: adj. Having the necessary ability or skill.
simple_examples: Noah has worked at this job for a long time and is a competent engineer.

ru: adj. Enhancing or completing another.
simple_examples: The artist and the engineer have skills that are complementary in the project.

ru: n. The state of being intricate or complicated.
simple_examples: The complexity of the 1,000 piece puzzle made it challenging.

ru: v. To create or write.
simple_examples: Jordan plans to compose a new symphony.
She composed a heartfelt letter to her grandmother.
advanced_example: The poet composed the collection over several years, revising each piece multiple times.

ru: v. To intensify or combine.
simple_examples: The traffic was compounded by bad weather.

ru: v. To consist of or include.
simple_examples: The book comprises ten chapters.

ru: v. To hide or keep secret.
simple_examples: Luca tried to conceal his disappointment.

ru: v. To admit or yield.

ru: v. To form an idea or concept.

ru: adj. Causing worry or distress.
simple_examples: The news about the approaching hurricane is quite concerning.

ru: n. The state of something.
simple_examples: The car I bought is in excellent condition.

ru: adj. Feeling sure or self-assured.
simple_examples: Michael Jordan is confident in his abilities as a basketball player.
She felt confident about her presentation.
advanced_example: Despite the challenges, the team remained confident that they could meet the deadline.

ru: adj. Combined in a misleading way.
simple_examples: The two issues were conflated in the argument.

ru: v. To comply with rules or expectations.
simple_examples: The alternative rocker refuses to conform to societal norms.

ru: n. General agreement.
simple_examples: The team finally reached a consensus on the decision.

ru: adj. Acting in the same way over time.

ru: adj. Easily noticed or standing out.

ru: adj. Occurring continuously.

ru: adj. Causing disagreement or debate.
simple_examples: Politics are highly contentious these days.

ru: adj. Dependent on something else.
simple_examples: Our family ski trip is contingent on the weather.
